To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the toxicity of heavy metals to anaerobic biodegradation of organic compounds is dependent on the types of organic compounds and the metals.

the bioactivities of acetate- and/or propionate-degrading anaerobic granules are less affected than those of starch- and/or benzoate-degradation granules, and that the toxicity of heavy metals on anaerobic bacteria follows the order: zinc > chromium > cadmium > copper > nickel.

(1) the methanogenic activity was inhibited by heavy metals in the order of zinc > nickel > chromium > copper > cadinium; (2) acetate- and starch-degrading biogarnules exhibited higher resistance than propionate- and benzoatdegrading ones; (3) heavy metals from electroplate effluent inhibited the bioactivities of the fermentative bacteria more than those in methanogens or acetogens; and (4) acetate conversion was a one-step process
In summary, our research is concerned with
the toxicity of five common electroplating metals on the bioactivity of anaerobic UASB bioreactors treating acetate, propioate, starch and benzote.
the effect of heavy metals on the activity of bioggranules in UASB reactors, which may provide useful information for the design of anaerobic wastewater treatments.
the effects of heavy metals commonly found at electroplating effluents on the bioactivity of methanogenic bacteria in the UASB reactor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bioactivity of anaerobic bacteria is more sensitive to zinc and nickel, and less sensitive to chromium and cadmium.
the toxicity of heavy metals to the anaerobic granules was in the following descending orders: acetate > propionate > starch > benzoate.
the toxicity of electroplating metals to the bioggranules treating different types of wastewater was in the following order: zinc > chromium > cadmium > nickel > copper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bioactivity of UAB granules is more sensitive to electroplating metal than that of the suspended biomass, and acetate- and starch-degrading granules are more tolerant to the heavy metals than the propionate- and benzoatdegrading ones.
the bioactivities of the fermentative/acidogens are more sensitive to the heavy metals than the bioactivities of acetogens and methogens.
the bioactivities of anaerobic bacteria, particularly those of fermentative/ acidogenic bacteria, can be inhibited by the heavy metals in electroplating effluents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to minimize the inhibition of heavy metals on anaerobic wastewater treatments, it is important to select the appropriate substrate and operating conditions for the treatment of electroplating effluents.
the toxicity of heavy metals on methanogenic activity is not only dependent on the type of wastewater but also on the type of metal.
the presence of metals in the wastewater will affect the performance of the UASB reactor treating the wastewater.
